To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribosides (AICAr, AICAr-related compounds, and AICAr metabolites) potentiates transport of reduced folate and antifolate substrates for the reduced folate transporter and their subsequent metabolism.

AICAr, the reduced form of the purine precursor AICAr, potentiates both influx and polyglutamate formation of reduced folates (e.g., [(3)H]-5-methyltetrahydrofolate) and MTX and other anticancer antifolate drugs in a variety of cell lines, and that this potentiation is mediated by the reduced folate transporter (RFC) in a dihydrofolate reduction and AICAr metabolism-dependent manner.

5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribosides (AICAr, AICArdR, and AICAr) are the first small molecules that potentiate RFC transport of reduced folate and antifoltes, and their subsequent metabolism to more biologically potent polyglutamate derivatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism of action for AICAr that is mediated via the RFC.
the mechanism by which AICAr potentiation of MTX transport and metabolism is achieved.
the regulation of folate transport and its role in the regulation of folates and antitumor folate antagonists in the human body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AICAr potentiates both RFC-mediated influx of antifolates and their polyglutamylation by a mechanism that does not require de novo protein synthesis.
AICAr is a new and unique pharmacologic agent that potentiates RFC activity and that this may be therapeutically useful.
AICAr is a novel regulator of RFC activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AICAr potentiates RFC activity and that the RFC is the major mediator of the potentiation.
AICAr potentiates both influx and metabolism of antifolates, but not folates, by the RFC, and that potentiation is mediated by effects of AICAr on the RFC itself.
AICAr is a potentiation factor for the RFC and that the mechanism of action is likely to involve inhibition of folate reductase.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the folate/antitumor antifolate transporter with widest tissue distribution and highest activity, the reduced folate/carrier, is subject to posttranscriptional regulation by AICAr, a small molecule that is present in the diet and is an endogenous metabolite.
the RFC is a potential therapeutic target for the development of new anticancer agents.
the folate/antifo-late carrier is regulated by a small molecule, AICAr, that is present in the diet, is a normal constituent of the body, and has been used as a therapeutic agent.
